change_summary: scratch_guard.sh v1: du/df/quotas triple plus projected-write cap and group free-space floor; negative tests driven by environment variables
expected: All eight threshold branches refuse with their documented exit codes; in particular the group free-space branch exits 2 when free space is below KTG_GROUP_FREE_FAIL_BYTES.
observed: 6 of 8 cases matched. Verbatim, from the run: '### case B: group free below the 1 TiB floor (expect exit 2) ###' ... 'scratch_guard: OK  used=7558579007 B  projected_total=29033415487 B  group_free=2380026322944 B' / 'exit=0'; and '### case C: warn floor only (expect exit 0 + WARNING) ###' produced the plain OK line with no WARNING. Evidence results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/data_budget/guard_exit_contract.txt (superseded run; the failing transcript is quoted here because the file was regenerated by the fix).
root_cause: budget.env assigns KTG_GROUP_FREE_FAIL_BYTES and KTG_GROUP_FREE_WARN_BYTES unconditionally (no ${VAR:-default} form), and scratch_guard.sh sources it AFTER the caller's environment is set, so the test's environment override was overwritten by the constants file and the guard evaluated the production floors against production free space. The two cases therefore measured nothing; they did not detect a broken branch, they never reached it.
fix_hypothesis: Keep the constants non-overridable from loose environment variables (that is the security property the guard needs) and instead make the constants FILE selectable: source ${KTG_BUDGET_ENV:-$HERE/budget.env}, print which file was used, and commit three fixture constants files under codes/data_budget/tests/ so each refusal branch is driven by an explicit file rather than by an env var the guard is designed to ignore.
next_hypothesis: Candidate failure_mode tag for this class: 'test_hook_shadowed' - the harness set a knob the code under test deliberately ignores, so the assertion passed vacuously.
notes: First instance of this class in this mission; logged as uncategorized_numerical per the self-correction protocol with a candidate tag in next_hypothesis. Domain 'numerical' is the closest of the three allowed values for a storage-accounting artifact; the trial is byte arithmetic against measured filesystem state. No result or knowledge row appended here: candidates are staged at results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/data_budget/candidate_rows.json for an independent validator.

change_summary: prune_retention.py v1: fixed retention rules plus a --target-bytes rolling mode that deletes oldest-first until the mission root is under a target
expected: Rolling mode may relax the keep-N floors when the mission root is over budget, but must never leave the loop without a training window: at least one shuffleddata dir and at least one selfplay generation survive, and no selfplay generation is removed while a retained shuffleddata dir could still reference its rows.
observed: On the synthetic tree, `prune_retention.py --root $T --target-bytes 2000000` planned 6 paths / 900000 B, verbatim: 'WOULD-REMOVE 200000 B .../loop/selfplay/gen3', 'WOULD-REMOVE 200000 B .../loop/selfplay/gen4', 'WOULD-REMOVE 200000 B .../loop/selfplay/gen5', 'WOULD-REMOVE 100000 B .../loop/shuffleddata/20260904-000000', 'WOULD-REMOVE 100000 B .../loop/shuffleddata/20260905-000000', 'WOULD-REMOVE 100000 B .../loop/shuffleddata/20260906-000000' - i.e. all three surviving selfplay generations and all three retained shuffle windows. The plan was a dry run, so nothing was deleted.
root_cause: The rolling loop iterated a single pool of (mtime, path) over shuffleddata and selfplay together and applied only two guards: a shuffleddata survivor count computed against shuf_all (which includes the young dir, so it permitted all old dirs to go) and a selfplay guard comparing each generation's mtime against oldest_retained_shuf computed BEFORE the rolling deletions. It never consulted the fixed keep-N floors, so the generations the fixed rule had deliberately kept became free candidates.
fix_hypothesis: Split rolling mode into two ordered passes with explicit hard minima that are separate constants from the keep-N floors: first drop shuffle windows oldest-first down to ROLLING_MIN_SHUFFLE_DIRS = 1 survivor, then RECOMPUTE the oldest retained window from the post-pass state and only then drop selfplay generations older than it, down to ROLLING_MIN_SELFPLAY_GENERATIONS = 1; warn and stop rather than crossing either minimum.
next_hypothesis: Candidate failure_mode tag for this class: 'retention_floor_bypass' - a best-effort optimisation loop was allowed to override the invariants the deterministic rules had just established.
notes: A different class from the iteration-1 partial (that one was a vacuous test; this one is a planner that violated its own invariant), so it is logged as a first instance of its own class with a candidate tag rather than triggering the second-instance module edit - editing phys-agentic-loop/_common/error_database.py is a framework change and outside this packet. Caught in dry run before any --apply; no data was lost. Evidence results/ktg/paper_1902.10565/evidence/data_budget/retention_synthetic_test.txt (regenerated after the fix; the failing plan is quoted verbatim above).

change_summary: attempted the coordinator-requested claim-ledger transition o04_scratch_budget -> status in_progress
expected: o04_scratch_budget moves to status in_progress while the guard lands, then to discharged once a result row exists.
observed: python3 phys-agentic-loop/_common/claims_database.py append rejected the row, verbatim: "ValueError: status='in_progress' not in ('open', 'discharged', 'waived') for kind='obligation'" raised at phys-agentic-loop/_common/ledgers/claims_database.py:106 in validate.
root_cause: in_progress belongs to the CLAIM status vocabulary; the obligation vocabulary is exactly open / discharged / waived (claims_database.py describe-fields: 'claim: open/in_progress/admitted/refuted/withdrawn; obligation: open/discharged/waived; assumption: active/relaxed/retired'). There is no intermediate obligation state by design.
fix_hypothesis: Re-append o04_scratch_budget at status open with the statement corrected to the 500 GiB decision and the partial progress recorded in notes, and leave the discharge to the validator: discharged_by is REQUIRED and is checked to exist, and the result row that would satisfy it does not exist yet because a worker must not append result rows for its own work. Conjunct (b) of o04 - the loop wrapper actually calling the guard - is also still unmet.
next_hypothesis: Candidate failure_mode tag for this class: 'status_vocabulary_mismatch' - a status valid for one ledger kind was applied to another.
notes: The instruction to set o04 in_progress is not satisfiable under the schema; reported back rather than worked around. No bypass flag was used.
